newsitem.title: CHINA: China to step up war on smuggling of oil products.
newsitem.headline: China to step up war on smuggling of oil products.

text.p: A top Chinese official has called for tougher measures to halt the smuggling of petroleum products along the nation's coast, the People's Daily said on Wednesday.

"Authorities at all levels in the coastal regions must make breakthroughs in halting the smuggling of oil products and other key items as part of our anti-smuggling campaign in the second half of this year," the newspaper quoted Vice-Premier Li Lanqing as saying.
Leaders of state enterprises and government departments which organised or engaged in smuggling could face expulsion from the party or even the long arm of the law, he said.
"Party and government organs at all levels must learn of the danger posed by smuggling," Li told a conference on anti-smuggling efforts.
He said smuggling by some state-owned companies, collective enterprises and even foreign-funded firms was a serious economic threat.
Many state oil refineries have complained bitterly of competition from cheaper, smuggled diesel fuel, which has led to reduced sales of their own products and even losses.
Industry officials say diesel fuel smugglers can save as much as $50 per tonne in import duties and other taxes.
About one million tonnes of diesel have been smuggled into China this year, taking advantage of higher state-set domestic prices, state media have said.
